question_text: Estimate the amount of heat (in J) required to raise 2 kg of (a) $\alpha$ - iron, (b) graphite, and (c) polypropylene from room temperature ($25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$) to $100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Give your answer as a tuple (heat for $\alpha$ - iron, heat for graphite, heat for polypropylene).The units of each required answer are (J, J, J), respectively.
response:
Using $Q = mc\Delta T$ with $m = 2\,\text{kg}$ and $\Delta T = 100 - 25 = 75\,\text{K}$, and the room-temperature specific heat capacities (Callister):

- $\alpha$-iron: $c_p \approx 448\,\text{J/(kg·K)}$
- graphite: $c_p \approx 707\,\text{J/(kg·K)}$
- polypropylene: $c_p \approx 1925\,\text{J/(kg·K)}$

$$Q_{\text{Fe}} = 2 \times 448 \times 75 = 67{,}200\,\text{J}$$
$$Q_{\text{graphite}} = 2 \times 707 \times 75 = 106{,}050\,\text{J}$$
$$Q_{\text{PP}} = 2 \times 1925 \times 75 = 288{,}750\,\text{J}$$

$$\boxed{(67200,\ 106050,\ 288750)}$$
